title: Can We Build Nuclear Reactors and Nuclear-Electric Propulsion Systems from Lunar Resources?
content: The lunar environment imposes challenging conditions for the generation and storage of electrical power that will be essential to support any lunar infrastructure, both human and robotic. In particular, lunar industrialisation will be required for permanent human occupation and to support the growth of robotic assets on the Moon, though it is worth noting that universal construction does not require a human presence. Nuclear reactors are an obvious solution but transport from Earth to the Moon is expensive as lunar infrastructure grows. We review the state-of-the-art of terrestrial and space nuclear reactors and find that advanced technology based on exotic materials to enhance reactor efficiency are not compatible with lunar reactor production where material resources are restricted. We then examine how nuclear reactors may be constructed from lunar resources within a set of constraints imposed by lunar industrial capabilities. We suggest that Magnox nuclear reactors, although a mature technology, are a practical possibility that may be leveraged and fuelled from lunar resources. From the vantage of the Moon, Magnox reactors may be married to water-propelled or Mg-propelled Hall effect thrusters, also manufactured and fuelled from lunar resources, opening up access to nuclear-electric propulsion (NEP) technology constructed in-situ.
